project.name: AI-Agent-Evals-Course
project.description: AI Evals in Practice: a 6-week course built around one Pronto grocery support demo agent, one eval dataset family, and browser-based eval tools.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: This file defines the core logic and tool-use capabilities of the Pronto customer service agent, serving as the primary application being evaluated throughout the course. It includes safety checks, refund processing rules, and a demo mode for testing without API keys.

nodes.name: build_pronto_eval_sets.py
nodes.summary: This script generates deterministic evaluation and regression datasets by packaging hand-authored support scenarios into structured CSV files with unique IDs and metadata. It ensures consistent testing data for both normal operations and known failure modes like adversarial attacks.

nodes.name: generate_pronto_tickets.py
nodes.summary: This script demonstrates synthetic data generation by filling hand-written templates with randomized customer and order data to create a realistic set of support tickets. It is used in the course to teach how to create diverse test cases for agent evaluation.

nodes.name: export_otel.py
nodes.summary: This utility script instruments the agent to export execution traces in OpenTelemetry format, allowing students to visualize agent-tool interactions without needing external API keys. It facilitates deep-dive error analysis by recording nested spans for every agent turn and tool call.

nodes.name: starter.py
nodes.summary: This starter script provides a workflow for running a batch of test inputs through the agent and generating a CSV file for manual pass/fail annotation. It helps students establish a baseline for human-in-the-loop evaluation and trace review.

nodes.name: judge_stats.py
nodes.summary: This statistical helper calculates bias-corrected pass rates and 95% confidence intervals to help students understand the reliability of LLM-based judges. It uses bootstrap resampling to estimate the true performance of an agent when the judge itself may be biased.

nodes.name: starter.py
nodes.summary: This script provides a framework for implementing and validating LLM judges using specific rubrics for policy adherence, escalation, and tool accuracy. It includes utility functions to calculate Cohen's Kappa and agreement matrices between LLM judges and human labels.

nodes.name: starter.py
nodes.summary: Implements and scores safety guardrails using regex, LLM judges, and hybrid approaches to detect adversarial attacks. It calculates catch rates and over-blocking metrics to evaluate safety performance.

nodes.name: pilot_scenarios.py
nodes.summary: Filters synthetic test scenarios by ensuring they can distinguish between a high-performing agent and a deliberately weakened one. This process helps build a golden set of discriminative evaluation cases.

nodes.name: starter.py
nodes.summary: Defines the schema and workflow for creating, validating, and uploading a RAG evaluation dataset to LangSmith. It focuses on establishing a versioned golden set for consistent model testing.

nodes.name: starter.py
nodes.summary: Uses RAGAS metrics and statistical bootstrap testing to compare different RAG configurations and measure improvements. It helps identify specific failures in retrieval or generation through quantitative analysis.

nodes.name: starter.py
nodes.summary: Scores agent tool-use trajectories against expected action sequences using property-based validation. It checks for required tool calls, forbidden actions, and correct execution order.

nodes.name: cost_model.py
nodes.summary: Analyzes the trade-off between agent accuracy and operational cost using a Pareto frontier model. It compares different configurations to find the most cost-effective balance for production deployment.

tour.title: How the Pronto agent works
tour.description: Start at the agent README, then read agent.py: the CustomerServiceAgent class, its four tools (get_order_status, lookup_policy, issue_refund, escalate_to_human), and the policy checks that gate refunds. End with the Week 3 guardrails starter to see how safety gets enforced around the same tools.
tour.languageLesson: Tool-calling agents centralize policy in wrapper functions (like issue_refund) so every path — demo, traced, or guarded — enforces the same rules.

tour.title: Week 1 student journey: from inputs to taxonomy
tour.description: Follow a student through Week 1: the 30 supplied inputs, the instrumented starter that runs them, export_otel.py which captures real OTLP traces with zero API keys, the Trace Viewer used to annotate them, and the taxonomy that comes out the other end.
tour.languageLesson: OpenTelemetry spans form parent-child trees: one trace per conversation, one span per agent turn or tool call.

tour.title: From judge to production gate
tour.description: Trace the course’s through-line: judge_stats.py bias-corrects a judge from 40 hand labels, the Judge Calibration Game teaches the same metrics interactively, cost_model.py trades accuracy against dollars on a Pareto frontier, and Week 6 turns it all into CI gates and production monitoring.
tour.languageLesson: A judge is only as good as its calibration: bias correction (Rogan-Gladen) plus bootstrap confidence intervals turn a raw pass rate into a decision-grade metric.
